definitions.gloss: to trigger; to induce; to cause; to provoke
definitions.explanation: To cause something (usually negative) to occur as a consequence. Often used in medical, scientific, and news contexts for events that set off a chain reaction or bring about an undesirable outcome.

examples.japanese: ストレスが{病気|びょうき}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する。
{大雨|おおあめ}が{土砂崩|どしゃくず}れを{誘発|ゆうはつ}する{恐|おそ}れがある。
examples.english: There is a risk that heavy rain will trigger landslides.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つの{事故|じこ}が{連鎖的|れんさてき}に{別|べつ}の{事故|じこ}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}して、{大規模|だいきぼ}な{渋滞|じゅうたい}が{発生|はっせい}した。
examples.english: One accident triggered a chain of other accidents, causing a major traffic jam.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
A が B を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (A triggers/induces B)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事故|じこ}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (to trigger an accident)
- {病気|びょうき}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (to induce illness)
- アレルギーを{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (to trigger allergies)
- {地震|じしん}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (to trigger an earthquake)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引|ひ}き{起|お}こす: To cause, to bring about — more general and common in everyday speech.
- {招|まね}く: To invite, to bring upon oneself — implies the cause was avoidable or negligent.
- {促|うなが}す: To urge, to promote — neutral, often positive, unlike {誘発|ゆうはつ} which tends toward negative outcomes.
